title: Locals in a stack frame
description:
Write a function that keeps an array in its own stack frame.

```
Five numbers: 3 9 1 7 5
sorted: 1 3 5 7 9
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
ask:    db      "Five numbers: ", 0

        section .text
read_sorted:
        push    rbp
        mov     rbp, rsp
        sub     rsp, 48
        ; TODO
        leave
        ret

_start:
        lea     rdi, [rel ask]
        call    print_str
        call    read_sorted

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: After `push rbp`, `rsp` is 16-byte aligned again (the `call` pushed 8, `push rbp` another 8), so subtract a multiple of 16 (lesson 5.03).
Keep the loop counters in `rbx` and `r12`, pushed after `rbp` and popped before `leave`; then `sub rsp` must still keep the stack aligned.
requirements: `read_sorted()` reserves 5 × 8 bytes with `sub rsp, 48` (keeping alignment), reads into it, sorts it with insertion sort, and prints it.
Address the locals as `[rbp - 8]`, `[rbp - 16]`, ... or `[rsp + i*8]`.
`leave` and `ret` at the end; callee-saved registers you use are pushed and popped.
stretch: Take the count as an argument and use `sub rsp, rax` (rounded up to 16) for the space.
